new_statements.quote: [ë] en CV accentué⁵ : /pè/ [pë] «être cuit» — [ə] en CV non accentué⁶ : /pè/ [pə̀] «ils» […] ⁵ La distinction entre syllabe accentuée et syllabe non accentuée n'est pertinente que pour les variantes du phonème /e/ en syllabe CV. (p. 20) […] 1.3. Tons. La langue kar comporte un système de trois tons: ton bas […], ton moyen […], ton haut […]. Ces trois tons ponctuels se réalisent soit sur un lexème verbal […] soit sur un lexème nominal dans le composé épithétique […] soit sur un morphème grammatical. (p. 21)
new_statements.translation: [ë] in an accented CV syllable: /pè/ [pë] 'be cooked' — [ə] in an unaccented CV syllable: /pè/ [pə̀] 'they' […] ⁵ The distinction between accented and unaccented syllable is relevant only for the variants of the phoneme /e/ in CV syllables. (p. 20) […] 1.3. Tones. The Kar language has a system of three tones: low tone, mid tone, high tone. These three level tones are realized either on a verbal lexeme, or on a nominal lexeme in the epithetic compound, or on a grammatical morpheme. (p. 21)

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (308 pp., pdfinfo title 'Kar Grammar-Unicode-final.doc', 2011) and; rendered PDF pages 20-21 (printed page numbers 20 and 21 match PDF page numbers). Quote check: p. 20 reads '- [ë] en CV accentué⁵ /pè/ [pë] «être cuit» / - [ə] en CV non accentué⁶ /pè/ [pə̀] «ils»' and fn 5 'La distinction entre syllabe accentuée et syllabe non accentuée n'est pertinente que pour les variantes du phonème /e/ en syllabe CV.' (fn 6 is a typesetting duplicate of fn 5, printed '6⁵ La distinction…'). p. 21 §1.3 Tons: 'La langue kar comporte un système de trois tons: - ton bas … - ton moyen … - ton haut …' and 'Ces trois tons ponctuels se réalisent soit sur un lexème verbal … soit sur un lexème nom…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kar is a three-level-tone language (L, M, H; five tone schemes on the phonological word: BB, MM, BM, HB, MB, with object-induced tonal replacement on verbs and postpositions). The grammar's only mention of stress is that an 'accented' vs 'unaccented' CV syllable conditions /e/ allophony ([ë] vs [ə]); the examples oppose a lexical verb monosyllable (accented) to a subject pronoun (unaccented), so the contrast is content word vs. function word/clitic rather than a positional rule. No rule for where word stress falls is given in any opened source; the 1979 phonology (chapters on syllable and phonological word not in the open extract) may say more.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the footnote restricts the accented/unaccented distinction to /e/ in CV syllables only.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (lexeme vs grammatical morpheme; 'mot phonologique'); the phonology chapter is a summary ('rappel') of Wichser & Bühler 1979, whose full text (78 pp.; HathiTrust search-only, htid uva.x001635739) could not be opened. Dictionary (Sagnon & Wichser 2012) marks base tones of citation forms and notes heavy tonal variation on verbs and pronouns, nothing on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: All first-hand sources describe the kar dialect of Tiéfora, the eastern Karaboro group (self-name Kai, language kar) = east2398 exactly. The western group (Syer/Tenyer, Tengrela) is a separate language, west2466 (Dombrowsky-Hahn 2015; Prost 1964); Wichser 1994 p. 6 says 'Sauf indication contraire, nous nous référerons uniquement au parler du groupe de l'est'. The earlier scan's 'Mills 1984' pointer is a misattribution: Mills 1984 is a phonology of Ivorian Senari (Cebaara) and Glottolog cites only its pp. xii-xx (classification) for Kar.

sources.note: Ch. 1 pp. 17-29: 16 consonants, vowels, three level tones (p. 21) with five tone schemes and object-to-verb tonal replacement (pp. 22-27), prosodic features nasalization/length/glottalization/labialization/palatalization (pp. 28-29). Stress only in fn 5 p. 20: accented vs unaccented CV syllable is relevant only to /e/ allophones ([ë] in accented /pè/ 'be cooked', [ə] in unaccented /pè/ 'they'); no placement rule. Page 20 visually verified.

sources.note: Intro pp. 5-6: entries repeated in brackets with base tone on every vowel (à low, ā mid, á high, plus mid-low, high-low, low-mid contours); 'Il y a beaucoup de variations dans la prononciation des tons, surtout sur les verbes et les pronoms'. Annex pp. 144-153 gives tonal paradigms of pronouns and verb aspect. Silent on stress/accent.
